name: @projexlight/sdk-agent-runtime
summary: AI agent isolation + execution runtime for ProjexCloud (P6A): declare an agent + its allowed tools + its vector namespace + a capability-token scope, then runs execute under that token with every tool call audited. Scope exceptions, replay, action journals, and cross-tenant leakage chaos tests are the contract — this SDK is the difference between 'a customer agent' and 'a tenant-isolated agent that survives an audit'.

endpoints.description: Mint a capability token scoped to (agent, tenant, persona, tool-set, vector-namespace, expires_at).
Server-side validate a token — does it still cover this tool call?
Revoke a capability token immediately (kill-switch for a runaway agent).
Replay an agent run from the journal for debugging / audit.
Fetch agent definition + active tokens + recent runs.
Start an agent run; returns run_id + initial token.
Fetch a run + its action journal + per-tool invocations.
Abort a run; outstanding tool calls cancel.
Record a scope exception (audit-grade; a tool call refused mid-run).
List vector namespaces for a tenant; agents read/write only their scoped namespace.

events.name: agents.token.minted.v1
events.description: Capability token minted; carries scope + expiry.

events.name: agents.token.revoked.v1
events.description: Token revoked; kill-switch for runaway runs.

events.name: agents.tool.invoked.v1
events.description: Tool call dispatched within a run; carries tool + arguments + result-hash + duration.

events.name: agents.scope.violation.detected.v1
events.description: Token-scope check refused a tool call; chaos-test signal + real-time abuse signal.

models.description: Per-agent row: name, allowed_tools, allowed_vector_namespaces, default_max_steps.
Per-(tenant, namespace) row — agents are scope-pinned to one namespace.
Per-run row: agent_id, persona_id, tenant_id, status, started_at, completed_at.
Per-token row: scope blob, expires_at, revoked_at.
Per-tool-call row: run_id, tool, args, result_hash, ok, duration_ms.
Per-run journal: full tool-call sequence + LLM messages for replay.

hooks.name: registerAgent
hooks.description: Create / update an agent definition (allowed tools, vector namespaces).

hooks.name: mintToken
hooks.description: Mint a capability token for a run; scope-pinned + expires.

hooks.name: startRun
hooks.description: Begin an agent run with a fresh token. Returns run_id.

hooks.name: invokeTool
hooks.description: Internal — every tool call routes through here for scope check + audit.

hooks.name: abortRun
hooks.description: Abort a run + revoke its token. Idempotent.

hooks.name: replayRun
hooks.description: Reconstruct a run from the action journal for audit / debug.

hooks.name: startChaosLeakage
hooks.description: AC-2 chaos test — periodic cross-tenant leakage probe (built-in; fails the deploy if regression).

scenarios.title: Register a customer-support agent (tools: search-kb + create-ticket)
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer wants an AI support agent on their portal; register it with the minimum tool-set + their tenant's vector namespace.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Agent definition row + emitted .agent.registered.v1. Future runs scope-check against this allowlist.

scenarios.title: Mint a capability token + start a run for a customer chat session
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer chat starts → mint a token scoped to this session + start an agent run under it.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Token + run rows; every tool call inside the run validates against this token. Token expires after 15 min — even if the agent tries to keep going.

scenarios.title: Agent tries a non-allowed tool → refusal + audit
scenarios.when_to_use: Agent hallucinates a `billing.refund` call; runtime refuses because the agent's tool-allowlist doesn't include it. The refusal is audited so red-team can replay.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Tool call refused. Run continues (with a refusal message back to the LLM). Audit chain has the violation for post-incident review.

scenarios.title: AC-2 chaos test — cross-tenant leakage probe
scenarios.when_to_use: Continuous integration safety: every hour, a synthetic run for tenant-A tries to read tenant-B's vector namespace. Token-scope must refuse. Failure halts the deploy pipeline.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Probe fires on cadence; emits .scope.violation.detected.v1 with chaos_test=true. Real ones (production agents) flagged separately. AC-2 SLO tracked.

scenarios.title: Replay a run for regulator audit
scenarios.when_to_use: Compliance regulator asks 'what did this agent do at time T'; replayRun reconstructs the full tool-call sequence + LLM messages from the action journal.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Full reproducible trace. Sufficient for GDPR Art-22 + EU AI Act decision-logic audit obligations.

compliance_posture.notes: Capability-token scope enforcement is the AC-2 chaos-test artifact — proves cross-tenant isolation under adversarial conditions. Action journals + replayRun answer the EU AI Act decision-trace requirement. Token revoke + abortRun are the killable-agent contract under NIST AI RMF Govern.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per chaos-test probe (background; included in SLO tier)
